title: Additivity of the root-of-unity embedding
statement:
Fix an integer $k \ge 1$ and let $\omega_k = e^{2\pi i/k}$ be the primitive $k$-th root of unity. For $a \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ write $\chi(a) = \omega_k^{a}$, where the exponent is the canonical representative of $a$ in $\{0, 1, \ldots, k-1\}$. Then for all $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
\chi(a + b) = \chi(a)\,\chi(b),
\]
so $\chi$ is a homomorphism from the additive group $\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ to the multiplicative group $\mathbb{C}^{\times}$.
hypotheses_covered: a and b range over Z/kZ
replaced:
For $a, b : \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$,
$\omega_k^{a+b} = \omega_k^a \cdot \omega_k^b$.
That is, $\texttt{ZkFourier.toOmega}$ is a group homomorphism from
$(\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}, +)$ to $(\mathbb{C}^\times, \cdot)$.
